rationale: Official release identity during the introduction; not evidence of benchmark performance.
The introduction explicitly promises published release examples. Preserve the sketch-to-3D reveal instead of cutting before its payoff.
Narration defines input and output; the official Claude Code demo shows an actual input being entered and the selected model.
Narration discusses long-session context and the mix of charges. Show the context/usage interface without treating the displayed percentage as a cache-price benchmark.
Official coding-workflow illustration during discussion of task steps; the separate article remains the evidence for GitHub's particular claim.
A visible implementation file illustrates a cross-file coding workflow. Narration explicitly calls its hypothetical login example an illustration, not our test.
The narrator asks viewers to inspect checks and changes rather than a finished screen; show the official code review and diff. Skip the first-frame presenter cut.
Narration explains command-line/tool work rather than quiz answers. Show real Claude Code interaction; no assertion that this demo is a Terminal Bench trial.

After source evaluation settings, the narration asks whether an output meets its specific requirements. The reconstruction's visible geometry and parameters illustrate that question, not a benchmark score.
The narrator recommends exposing underlying structure so output can be reviewed; the official exploded-parts view supplies a concrete visual analogy, not a financial table or our test.
At the instruction to look for inputs and verification, show camera/light reconstruction parameters through the finished Earthrise output.
Show a real before/after explanation while narration discusses clearer communication. Cursor's recommendation remains sourced separately.
The official demo visibly compares bug explanations, directly supporting the topic of reviewing clearer writing.

An official interactive explanation illustrates the instruction to explain unfamiliar terms. Begin on the interactive view rather than the title card. It is not substituted for the earlier billing-code evidence.
The educational visualization remains interactive while narration discusses following explanation instructions across a task.
The viewer sees a concrete follow-up instruction and model revision while narration discusses consistency across a whole task.
The actual medium-effort control and tooltip match the narrated model-setting explanation. Begin after the presenter shot.
The narrator distinguishes fast text from a usable completed output. Let the throw and block knockdown finish; this is not a speed measurement.
The practical payoff is usable, verifiable work. Show the produced step-by-step instructions rather than a generic model card.
The closing asks viewers to inspect a familiar task and its results; interactive simulation controls illustrate inspecting an output, not independent accuracy validation.
The conclusion asks whether a finished job works. Show the interactive throw through its landing; no cost or accuracy claim is inferred from this clip.
End on visible structural checking rather than an article; the narration says actual work decides whether a model remains useful.
